# Discovery-prep brief: Hyatt Hotels Corporation

Prepared 2026-10-25 for a first meeting. Every line cites its sources; lines the critic couldn't source were removed. Research by an AI agent from public web pages: check before quoting.

## Snapshot

- Hyatt Hotels Corporation (NYSE: H, Class A) is a hotel company operating 1,528 properties and 372,763 rooms across 83 countries as of December 31, 2025. [1][5]
- About 242,000 colleagues work across corporate, regional offices, and managed, franchised, owned, and leased properties; about 50,000 are directly employed by Hyatt. [2]
- The Luxury Portfolio includes Park Hyatt, Alila, Miraval, Impression by Secrets, and The Unbound Collection by Hyatt; a September 2025 release put it at nearly 125 hotels and more than 21,000 rooms. [3][9]
- Hyatt Hotels & Resorts is one of the businesses managed by the Pritzker family. [5]
- Playa rooms were removed from Hyatt's room count in the second half of 2025, so older Playa-based figures will not match current totals. [10]

## Recent news (last 12 months)

- Hyatt completed the $2 billion sale of the Playa Hotels & Resorts real estate portfolio (reported by Hotel Dive on January 5, 2026). [11]
- In December 2025, Hyatt sold its remaining 14 Playa properties to Tortuga Resorts and entered 50-year management agreements with Tortuga for 13 of the 14. [6][12][13][14][15]
- Hyatt reported a record pipeline of about 148,000 rooms as of year-end 2025 (announced January 26, 2026). [6][12][13][14][15]
- On May 28, 2026, Hyatt announced a $1 billion increase in share repurchase authorization and an illustrative financial outlook through 2028. [6][12][13][14][15]
- In Q2 2026 results (July 2026), the sale of Hyatt Grand Central New York was no longer expected to close in 2026, and Distribution adjusted EBITDA fell on temporary factors including Hurricane Melissa closures in Jamaica and softer 4-star demand in Mexico. [6][12][13][14][15]
- Hyatt will release third quarter 2026 results on October 29, 2026, which may change the picture shortly after the meeting. [6][12][13][14][15]

## What guests say (themes)

- Service inconsistency: guests report unhelpful, dismissive staff when complaints are raised, and a luxury environment with weak service makes the contrast the complaint. [16][17]
- Cleanliness and maintenance vary by property, with reports of stains, mold, musty odors, and severe in-room maintenance problems. [16][17][18][19]
- Value and fees are the most criticized area: high prices relative to the experience, unexpected charges, and hidden fees. [16][17][20][21]
- Location and amenities are frequent strengths, though pools and gyms are sometimes criticized. [18][19][20]
- Loyalty benefits are mixed; dynamic pricing and add-on charges can feel transactional, and some members feel let down. [17][21][22]

## Technology hints

- Property management system: Oracle OPERA Cloud was selected in September 2024 for more than 1,000 properties, migrating from on-premise Opera V5. [23]
- Central reservations: a trade article reports a deal with Sabre to adopt the SynXis CRS as its main CRS. [24]
- Digital engagement: a redesigned World of Hyatt mobile app (iOS and Android, loyalty members only) with Bluetooth digital keys. [25][26]
- Guest messaging: Medallia Zingle-powered intelligent messaging is being deployed across the portfolio. [26]
- Experiences integration: Way's platform and APIs integrate into Hyatt.com, the app, property websites, and FIND Experiences. [27]
- AI in use: proprietary AI values group business and an AI platform surfaces signals for hotel teams; generative AI powers search by personal intent. [28][29][30]

## Ten questions for the meeting

1. Which operational system of record does each property team use day to day, and how does OPERA Cloud integrate with the SynXis CRS and the loyalty platform?
2. How is the migration from Opera V5 to OPERA Cloud progressing across the more than 1,000 properties, and which properties are still on the old system?
3. Which teams own the AI signal platform that surfaces opportunities for hotel teams, and how do they measure whether a signal led to action?
4. How do guest complaints get logged, routed, and closed today, and which system holds that record?
5. Where do the service complaints about unhelpful staff originate: front desk, housekeeping, food and beverage, or guest messaging?
6. How are maintenance requests raised and tracked at property level, and who decides when a room is taken out of service?
7. How are fees and add-on charges set, and what internal checks exist before a guest sees a surprise charge?
8. What did the Playa transition to Tortuga change in the systems and workflows your teams use, and which parts are still shared?
9. How are owners currently using the vendor-spend and revenue tools, and what do owners say they still need?
10. What signals would tell you a loyalty member is at risk of feeling let down, and is that data available to the property team?

## Three use-case hypotheses (4-check test)

| Use case | Why | Felt | Would pay | Buildable in a week | First user known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guest complaint triage and routing | Reviews repeatedly describe dismissive handling of complaints and unresolved maintenance and fee issues. [16][22] | Probably | Unknown | Probably | Unknown |
| Property-level maintenance and cleanliness issue detection | Reviews cite mold, stains, and missed housekeeping, but public information on maintenance workflows is absent. [17][18][19] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |
| Fee and value transparency assistant for guests and staff | Value and hidden fees are the most criticized area, and loyalty members say add-on charges feel transactional. [16][17][20][21] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |

## Outreach email

> Hi, I'm writing to ask for a 30-minute discovery call. I've been reading public material on Hyatt's recent portfolio changes, the Playa transition, and the systems mentioned in its 2024 Oracle OPERA Cloud announcement. I'd like to learn how guest issues move from the property to the systems that handle them, and where your teams spend the most effort today. I'm not selling anything in this first call. Would any time in the next two weeks work for you? Thanks, Vamsi

# Discovery-prep brief: Club Med

Prepared 2026-10-25 for a first meeting. Every line cites its sources; lines the critic couldn't source were removed. Research by an AI agent from public web pages: check before quoting.

## Snapshot

- Club Med SAS is a Paris-headquartered tourism subsidiary; its majority owner is Fosun Tourism Group, the leisure unit of Fosun International. [1][2]
- Fosun's takeover was completed in 2015. [3]
- Club Med is an all-inclusive resort operator founded in 1950, with products including all-inclusive holidays, tours, and the Club Med 2 sailing yacht. [1][6][7][10]
- Its footprint is reported at 68 resorts in 40 countries across ownership, lease and management-contract structures, but counts vary by source (about 60 to 61 in 2026 reports). [1][4][5][10][11][12]
- Employee counts vary widely by source (about 14K to 29K), so headcount is unconfirmed. [4]

## Recent news (last 12 months)

- July 2025: Henri Giscard d'Estaing said Fosun ousted him as president; Fosun disputes his account. The dispute concerned possible relisting on the Paris Stock Exchange. [9]
- April 2026: The company set a goal of 100 villages within 10 years, implying roughly 40 openings. [10][16]
- April 20, 2026: The 2025 results release was published, reporting an average daily rate of €241, up 5% at constant exchange rates. [18][19][20]
- July 4, 2026: Club Med South Africa Beach & Safari opened. [17]
- July 2026: Club Med signed a strategic cooperation memorandum with Microsoft at its Paris headquarters. [31]
- September 17, 2026: Inauguration of its first South Africa resort is listed on the corporate news page. [18][19][20]
- November 2026: Club Med Borneo in Sabah, Malaysia is scheduled to open, with a 400-key rainforest property. [18][19][20]

## What guests say (themes)

- Guests praise warm, attentive service and staff who remember them, especially for children. [21][39]
- Activities and sports are a major draw, with more than 60 activities depending on the resort. [23][35]
- Food variety and buffet quality draw repeated criticism. [22][23]
- Slow or inattentive service appears at some properties. [24][25]
- Evening entertainment is mixed, with some resorts criticized. [26]
- Value for money, extra costs, and room upkeep recur as concerns. [21][24]

## Technology hints

- Events booking runs on a Salesforce-based app built by GoMeddo, used to schedule more than 1,000 business events a year. [27]
- Property management and group tools use UrVenue's PXMS platform. [28]
- The Group Itinerary Builder launched in April 2024 at Club Med Cancún. [29]
- The WhatsApp customer assistant was built on Azure OpenAI Service and covers 50% of conversations with Brazilian customers. [32]
- Club Med has a partnership with Thales and Google to secure sensitive HR data. [33]
- Windsor.ai was appointed for marketing attribution and data integration, though that article is about seven years old. [34]

## Ten questions for the meeting

1. Which system is the system of record for resort inventory and room status, and how does it connect to PXMS?
2. How is the Salesforce-based events booking app integrated with the booking and property systems?
3. What does the WhatsApp assistant currently handle, and what is its escalation path to human staff?
4. Which guest-facing channels exist today (app, website, booking engine), given that public information on them is missing?
5. How are Gold and Platinum pre-arrival touchpoints such as Easy Arrival run today, and who owns that data?
6. What are the current loyalty tier thresholds, given that sources conflict on them?
7. How do guest feedback and review data reach resort management, and how quickly?
8. Which resort-level decisions (food, activities, entertainment) are central and which are local?
9. How will the 100-village expansion and the Borneo and South Africa openings be staffed and systematized?
10. Who owns the Travel Agent Portal and tiered agent rewards, and how are agent bookings reconciled with direct ones?

## Three use-case hypotheses (4-check test)

| Use case | Why | Felt | Would pay | Buildable in a week | First user known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pre-arrival personalised messaging for loyalty members | Gold and Platinum members get pre-stay services that are natural points for personalised messages. [36][37][38] | Unknown | Unknown | Probably | Probably |
| Activity recommendation for guests across resorts | A broad activity catalogue plus guest interest in activities may support recommendations. [23][35] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |
| Guest feedback triage for food and service issues | Repeated complaints about food variety, service speed, and room upkeep could be surfaced earlier. [21][22][23][24][25] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |

## Outreach email

> Hello,
>
> I'm reaching out to ask for a 30-minute discovery call. I'd like to learn how Club Med's guest and operations teams currently handle bookings, pre-arrival communication, and guest feedback, and where those processes create the most friction.
>
> I've read the public material on your recent systems work, including the WhatsApp assistant and the events booking app, and I'd like to hear from your team what matters most day to day.
>
> Would a 30-minute call in the next two weeks work for you? I can adjust to your schedule.
>
> Thanks,
> Vamsi

# Discovery-prep brief: Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts

Prepared 2026-10-25 for a first meeting. Every line cites its sources; lines the critic couldn't source were removed. Research by an AI agent from public web pages: check before quoting.

## Snapshot

- Privately held luxury hotel and resort company; majority shareholder is Cascade Investment, L.L.C. (about 71.25%), with Kingdom Holding Company (23.75%) and the Sharp family (5%). [1][2]
- Headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. [3]
- Operates about 135 hotels and resorts and 61 residential properties in 47 countries per its January 2026 65th-anniversary release; older references cite 133 hotels and resorts. [1][8][9][10][12]
- Reports nearly 60,000 colleagues; third-party trackers report lower figures (about 49,000 to 43,000). [5][6][7]
- Roughly 60 additional projects are in development, with 65% of the pipeline including a residential component. [8][9][10][11]
- No reliable public breakdown by region or property type was found, and source counts conflict. [8][11]

## Recent news (last 12 months)

- Robert Fritz named Executive Chairman; Founder Isadore Sharp moves to Chairman Emeritus (date not stated in findings). [12][13]
- Berlin: Four Seasons agreed with Gruppo Statuto to take over management of Hotel de Rome; it operates as Hotel de Rome through 2026 and is to reopen as Four Seasons Hotel Berlin in 2027 after renovations (2025 press releases). [12][13][14]
- Sevilla, Spain: new hotel with Blasson announced, opening 2028 (2026). [14]
- Four Seasons Hotel Mykonos accepting reservations ahead of summer opening (May 2026). [1][12]
- Development update on October 20, 2026 covering 13 upcoming hotel and resort openings and reopenings across five regions, mostly 2027 and beyond. [8][11]
- Four Seasons Resort and Residences Puerto Rico opened November 2025; Venice Hotel Danieli is slated to reopen as a Four Seasons. [15]
- No reliable public reports found of financial or occupancy results, or sales or ownership changes, from October 2025 to October 2026. [1][12]

## What guests say (themes)

- Staff and spa facilities are the most praised aspects, with cleanliness and attentive service often commended, though lapses are mentioned. [16]
- Recurring complaint that service does not justify the premium price, with reviewers expecting a more elevated experience. [17]
- Check-in friction reported in more than one city (card declines in New York, a 20-minute check-in in Las Vegas). [18][19]
- Room and facility age and pool access are mixed points, including untouched bathrooms despite a 2020 renovation and pool waitlists. [17]

## Technology hints

- A 2000s-era announcement says OPERA Property Management System was selected for new properties; no current confirmation found. [20][21]
- A 2020 release describes a guest app for reservations and airport transfer requests via an on-call concierge. [21]
- A 2018 trade article says the chat service is staffed by people on property, not bots. [22]
- A 2018 CIO interview names Adobe for web and digital experience, and says the company uses Salesforce, Workday and Microsoft. [22][23]
- Vendor case studies (Medallia, Avero) claim Four Seasons uses their platforms; these are vendor marketing claims. [22][23][24]
- No booking engine or Preferred Partner platform details were found. [20]

## Ten questions for the meeting

1. Which systems do you treat as the system of record for reservations, guest profiles, and folios today, and which of them are run by the corporate team versus each property?
2. How much of the property management stack is still OPERA, and which hotels, if any, run a different PMS?
3. Where does check-in actually slow down, and what share of arrivals hit the card-decline or long-wait problems seen in guest reviews?
4. How do guest feedback signals from Medallia reach property leaders, and how quickly do they lead to a changed action?
5. What does a service failure cost you today, and who measures whether the premium price is justified at each hotel?
6. Which parts of the Berlin and Sevilla openings or the 13-property pipeline depend on systems work, and who owns that work?
7. How are the AI conference-assistant and interpretation tools in Kuala Lumpur being measured, and what would make them roll out to other properties?
8. How do the AI waste-tracking tools at Papagayo feed into food and cost decisions, and who acts on the data?
9. Which operational tasks do property teams spend the most hours on that are still manual, such as reconciling data across Adobe, Salesforce, and the PMS?
10. Which of the systems named in 2018 and 2020 sources have been replaced since, and who in IT or operations could confirm the current stack?

## Three use-case hypotheses (4-check test)

| Use case | Why | Felt | Would pay | Buildable in a week | First user known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Check-in and arrival friction reduction | Guest reviews report card declines and long check-ins in multiple cities, and the company has tested self check-in in Kuala Lumpur. [18][19][25] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |
| Guest feedback triage and service recovery | Recurring reviews about service versus price suggest feedback is not tied quickly to action; Medallia is already in use, so a layer on top may fit. [17][22][23] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |
| Kitchen food-waste analytics at buffet properties | A Four Seasons property already uses camera and scale tools for buffet waste, showing the cost problem is recognized. [27] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |

## Outreach email

> Hello,
>
> I would like to learn how Four Seasons approaches guest-facing operations and the systems behind them. Would you be open to a 30-minute discovery call in the coming weeks? I would like to hear which processes take the most effort today and where the current tools fall short.
>
> If useful, I can send a few specific questions in advance so the time is well spent.
>
> Thank you,
> Vamsi

## Sources

# Discovery-prep brief: Sandals Resorts International

Prepared 2026-10-25 for a first meeting. Every line cites its sources; lines the critic couldn't source were removed. Research by an AI agent from public web pages: check before quoting.

## Snapshot

- Sandals Resorts International is privately held by the Stewart family, and the company does not appear to be publicly traded. [1]
- Founded in 1981 by Gordon "Butch" Stewart; handles resort development, service standards, training and day-to-day operations. [2]
- Parent of five all-inclusive brands: Sandals Resorts, Beaches Resorts, Grand Pineapple Beach Resorts, Fowl Cay Resort and the Private Villas of Sandals & Beaches. Sandals is positioned for adults and couples; Beaches is the family-oriented brand. [3][4][9]
- Operates about 17 beachfront resorts across Jamaica, Antigua, Saint Lucia, The Bahamas, Barbados, Grenada, Curaçao and Saint Vincent and The Grenadines. Older sources cite 16, so the count may have changed. One Beaches property in Ocho Rios closed permanently on May 31, 2025. [5][8][9]
- Headcount sources disagree: about 13,324 (one workforce data provider, March 2026), 10,001+ (LinkedIn), and more than 18,000 (company statement reported by the Jamaica Gleaner). The Executive Chairman said in September 2026 it plans to add 7,000 jobs, some outside the Caribbean. [2][6][7]
- A deal with a 50% stake retained by the Stewart family had not closed as of October 1, 2026, and is expected to close in early 2027. [1]

## Recent news (last 12 months)

- March 2026: Sandals Resorts International committed US$200 million to reimagine Sandals Montego Bay, Sandals Royal Caribbean and Sandals South Coast, the three Jamaica resorts still closed after Hurricane Melissa. Work includes new accommodation categories, redesigned pools and new dining concepts. [12][13]
- Reopening dates set for late 2026: Sandals South Coast on November 18, 2026; the other two Jamaica resorts on December 18, 2026. [14][32]
- June 2026: Sandals Royal Caribbean is to debut as Sandals Caribbean Cay after the rename. [15]
- July 2026: Executive Chairman Adam Stewart described the rebuild as a continuation of the Sandals 2.0 strategy; the company said it secured permission to add 16 overwater bungalows at Sandals Montego Bay. [16]
- July 2026: Sandals announced travel advisor initiatives for Jamaica's 2026 Independence Day celebrations, including events in 25 U.S. cities and incentives and contests for advisors. [33]
- September 2026 (unverified): one source reports Royal Caribbean Group would take a 50% equity stake in Sandals for $3 billion, announced September 22, 2026. [17]

## What guests say (themes)

- Dining is the most consistent strength, especially specialty restaurants (seafood, sushi, wood-fired dishes). [18][19]
- Service is inconsistent: butler-level service is praised, while standard-room service ranges from smooth to slow, particularly at busy times. [18][19][20]
- Recurring complaints about food quality, room-service delays and value for money, with pricing often seen as not matching the experience. [20][21][22][23]
- Room condition is mixed; complaint boards report mold, disrepair and long waits. [23][24][25]

## Technology hints

- Property management was standardized on Infor Hotel Management System and Infor Enterprise Asset Management for Hospitality, per an older vendor case study (rollout from December 2012; the 2012-2013 timing makes this possibly outdated). [26]
- Loyalty program Sandals Select Rewards becomes Island Insiders Club on July 1, 2026; the upgraded resort app handles offers, excursions, balance payments and rewards. [27][28][29]
- The Sandals & Beaches app supports booking details, trip management, check-in and dining reservations, per a third-party guide. [31]
- Low-confidence third-party tech-stack lists include Optimizely A/B Testing, Microsoft Advertising, Movable Ink Personalization and YouTube. [30]

## Ten questions for the meeting

1. Which systems run reservations, property management, and guest messaging today, and how well do they connect to the Island Insiders Club app?
2. Since the 2012-2013 Infor rollout, what has been upgraded or replaced, and who owns that stack now?
3. How does the team handle guest feedback from Trustpilot and complaint boards today, and who acts on it?
4. Where do standard-room service delays most often originate: housekeeping, room service, or front desk?
5. How are room-service orders taken, routed to kitchens, and tracked for delays?
6. How are the Jamaica reopenings (November and December 2026) being planned operationally, and what systems support that?
7. How do travel advisors book and get support, and how is that differentiated from direct bookings?
8. How are staffing levels planned for the 7,000 new jobs, and what tools support hiring and training?
9. Which operational metrics (service standards, maintenance backlogs, food quality) does leadership review regularly?
10. What information is not reliably tracked today, such as headcount, property count, or guest satisfaction by property?

## Three use-case hypotheses (4-check test)

| Use case | Why | Felt | Would pay | Buildable in a week | First user known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guest feedback triage for service and maintenance issues | Recurring complaints about inconsistent service, mold, disrepair and wait times appear across public review sources. [20][21][22][24][25] | Probably | Unknown | Probably | Unknown |
| Travel advisor and guest booking support assistant | Support depends on booking channel, and the company is running advisor initiatives and an app with booking and check-in features. [31][33] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Probably |
| Room-service and kitchen order tracking | Food quality and room-service delays are repeated complaints; whether the operation has a tracking problem is not established. [20][21][22] | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |

## Outreach email

> Hello,
>
> I'm reaching out to ask for a 30-minute discovery call to learn how Sandals Resorts International handles guest service, property operations and reservations today, and where the work is hardest. I'd like to understand the systems you use and the reopening plans for the Jamaica resorts before we talk about anything specific.
>
> Would a 30-minute call in the next two weeks work for you? I can work around your schedule.
>
> Thank you,
> Vamsi

- Parent of five all-inclusive brands: Sandals Resorts, Beaches Resorts, Grand Pineapple Beach Resorts, Fowl Cay Resort and the Private Villas of Sandals & Beaches. Sandals is positioned for adults and couples; Beaches is the family-oriented brand. [3][4][9]
- Operates about 17 beachfront resorts across Jamaica, Antigua, Saint Lucia, The Bahamas, Barbados, Grenada, Curaçao and Saint Vincent and The Grenadines. Older sources cite 16, so the count may have changed. One Beaches property in Ocho Rios closed permanently on May 31, 2025. [5][8][9]
- Headcount sources disagree: about 13,324 (one workforce data provider, March 2026), 10,001+ (LinkedIn), and more than 18,000 (company statement reported by the Jamaica Gleaner). The Executive Chairman said in September 2026 it plans to add 7,000 jobs, some outside the Caribbean. [2][6][7]
- A deal with a 50% stake retained by the Stewart family had not closed as of October 1, 2026, and is expected to close in early 2027. [1]

## Recent news (last 12 months)

- March 2026: Sandals Resorts International committed US$200 million to reimagine Sandals Montego Bay, Sandals Royal Caribbean and Sandals South Coast, the three Jamaica resorts still closed after Hurricane Melissa. Work includes new accommodation categories, redesigned pools and new dining concepts. [12][13]
- Reopening dates set for late 2026: Sandals South Coast on November 18, 2026; the other two Jamaica resorts on December 18, 2026. [14][32]
- June 2026: Sandals Royal Caribbean is to debut as Sandals Caribbean Cay after the rename. [15]
- July 2026: Executive Chairman Adam Stewart described the rebuild as a continuation of the Sandals 2.0 strategy; the company said it secured permission to add 16 overwater bungalows at Sandals Montego Bay. [16]
- July 2026: Sandals announced travel advisor initiatives for Jamaica's 2026 Independence Day celebrations, including events in 25 U.S. cities and incentives and contests for advisors. [33]
- September 2026 (unverified): one source reports Royal Caribbean Group would take a 50% equity stake in Sandals for $3 billion, announced September 22, 2026. [17]

## What guests say (themes)

- Dining is the most consistent strength, especially specialty restaurants (seafood, sushi, wood-fired dishes). [18][19]
- Service is inconsistent: butler-level service is praised, while standard-room service ranges from smooth to slow, particularly at busy times. [18][19][20]
- Recurring complaints about food quality, room-service delays and value for money, with pricing often seen as not matching the experience. [20][21][22][23]
- Room condition is mixed; complaint boards report mold, disrepair and long waits. [23][24][25]

## Technology hints

- Property management was standardized on Infor Hotel Management System and Infor Enterprise Asset Management for Hospitality, per an older vendor case study (rollout from December 2012; the 2012-2013 timing makes this possibly outdated). [26]
- Loyalty program Sandals Select Rewards becomes Island Insiders Club on July 1, 2026; the upgraded resort app handles offers, excursions, balance payments and rewards. [27][28][29]
- The Sandals & Beaches app supports booking details, trip management, check-in and dining reservations, per a third-party guide. [31]
- Low-confidence third-party tech-stack lists include Optimizely A/B Testing, Microsoft Advertising, Movable Ink Personalization and YouTube. [30]

## Ten questions for the meeting

1. Which systems run reservations, property management, and guest messaging today, and how well do they connect to the Island Insiders Club app?
2. Since the 2012-2013 Infor rollout, what has been upgraded or replaced, and who owns that stack now?
3. How does the team handle guest feedback from Trustpilot and complaint boards today, and who acts on it?
4. Where do standard-room service delays most often originate: housekeeping, room service, or front desk?
5. How are room-service orders taken, routed to kitchens, and tracked for delays?
6. How are the Jamaica reopenings (November and December 2026) being planned operationally, and what systems support that?
7. How do travel advisors book and get support, and how is that differentiated from direct bookings?
8. How are staffing levels planned for the 7,000 new jobs, and what tools support hiring and training?
9. Which operational metrics (service standards, maintenance backlogs, food quality) does leadership review regularly?
10. What information is not reliably tracked today, such as headcount, property count, or guest satisfaction by property?

## Three use-case hypotheses (4-check test)

| Use case | Why | Felt | Would pay | Buildable in a week | First user known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guest feedback triage for service and maintenance issues | Recurring complaints about inconsistent service, mold, disrepair and wait times appear across public review sources. [20][21][22][24][25] | Probably | Unknown | Probably | Unknown |
| Travel advisor and guest booking support assistant | Support depends on booking channel, and the company is running advisor initiatives and an app with booking and check-in features. [31][33] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Probably |
| Room-service and kitchen order tracking | Food quality and room-service delays are repeated complaints; whether the operation has a tracking problem is not established. [20][21][22] | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |

# Discovery-prep brief: Hyatt Hotels Corporation

Prepared 2026-10-25 for a first meeting. Every line cites its sources; lines the critic couldn't source were removed. Research by an AI agent from public web pages: check before quoting.

## Snapshot

- Hyatt Hotels Corporation is a public company (NYSE: H, Class A) headquartered in Chicago at 150 North Riverside Plaza. [3][4]
- As of December 31, 2025 it operated about 1,528 properties and 372,763 rooms across 83 countries; about 242,000 colleagues, roughly 50,000 directly employed by Hyatt. [1][2]
- Brands named in aggregator listings include Park Hyatt, Grand Hyatt, Hyatt Regency, Andaz, Alila, Thompson, Hyatt Centric, Hyatt Place, Hyatt House and JdV by Hyatt. [1]
- Wikipedia notes the business is one of those managed by the Pritzker family. [4]

## Recent news (last 12 months)

- Dec 2025: Hyatt named Tamara Lohan interim Global Brand Leader for its luxury brands. [10][11][12][13]
- Jan 2026: Hyatt announced a pipeline of approximately 148,000 rooms as of year-end 2025. [10][11][12][13]
- Feb 2026: Hyatt reported a small 2025 net loss, Adjusted EBITDA of $1.16B, and 2026 Adjusted Free Cash Flow guidance of $580–$630M. [10][11][12][13]
- Jul 2026: Q2 comparable system-wide hotels RevPAR increased 5.9% year over year; full-year RevPAR growth guidance is 3.5% to 4.5%. [6][10][11][12][13][14]
- Sep 30, 2026: Hyatt announced a series of openings and projects for Essentials Portfolio brands in the United States. [6][14]
- Oct 29, 2026: Q3 2026 results are scheduled, before market open; this falls after today's date (Oct 25, 2026). [15]

## What guests say (themes)

- Service and fees are the main complaint: reviewers cite unhelpful, dismissive staff when problems arise, plus hidden fees and surprise charges. [16]
- Room upkeep varies by property: worn furniture, weak air conditioning and soiled bedding recur, though some guests call rooms clean and comfortable. [17][18][19]
- Strengths cited are location, friendly staff and breakfast at some hotels. [16]
- Guests describe dynamic pricing that erodes point value, paid add-ons at odds with elite status, and little flexibility when something goes wrong. [20]

## Technology hints

- Sabre's SynXis Central Reservation System is reported to become the main CRS for Hyatt hotels beginning in 2024. [21]
- Oracle OPERA Cloud is reported as the chosen property management system for the global hotel portfolio. [22]
- Hyatt will integrate Way's platform and APIs across Hyatt.com, the World of Hyatt app, property websites and World of Hyatt Find. [23]
- Hyatt rebuilt hyatt.com search around natural-language, intent-based queries; management reports improved booking conversion and revenue. [25][26][27]
- Hyatt staff will use ChatGPT Enterprise across finance, marketing and operations. [28][29]

## Ten questions for the meeting

1. Which systems do your central reservations, PMS, revenue management and loyalty each run on today, and where do they connect?
2. How do owners and franchisees get property data (PMS costs, vendor spend, revenue signals), and which parts are manual?
3. Where do guest service complaints about unhelpful staff and fees originate in the workflow: front desk, reservations, or post-stay support?
4. How are hidden fees and add-on charges set, and who approves changes to them?
5. What does the hotel team do today when a guest escalates a problem, and what tools do they have to resolve it on the spot?
6. How is the AI platform that surfaces revenue signals for hotel teams used day to day, and what do teams act on versus ignore?
7. How do you measure the conversion lift from the natural-language search, and what has been hard to measure?
8. Which properties are in the 2026 openings and Essentials conversions, and what onboarding work does each new property need on systems?
9. What is the process for room condition inspections across properties, and where does upkeep data get recorded?
10. Which part of the 2026 plan (RevPAR, pipeline, cash flow targets) is most constrained by operations or systems today?

## Three use-case hypotheses (4-check test)

| Use case | Why | Felt | Would pay | Buildable in a week | First user known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AI-assisted guest service triage and resolution for fee and problem complaints | Reviews repeatedly cite unhelpful staff, surprise charges and poor handling of complaints. [16] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |
| Owner-side property systems and vendor spend optimization assistant | Hyatt reports owner-side PMS cost reduction and AI tools for vendor spending and revenue management. [26][27][28][29] | Unknown | Probably | Unknown | Unknown |
| Property upkeep and room condition tracking across hotels | Room condition complaints vary by property and recur for furniture, A/C and bedding. [17][18][19] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |

## Outreach email

> Hi,
>
> I'm looking to learn more about how Hyatt approaches guest service, property systems and owner tooling as the 2026 openings ramp up. Would you have 30 minutes in the coming weeks for a discovery call? I'd like to hear how your teams work today and what gets in the way, before proposing anything.
>
> If a time works, tell me a few options and I'll fit around your schedule. Happy to send a short list of topics beforehand.
>
> Thanks,
> Vamsi

# Discovery-prep brief: Club Med

Prepared 2026-10-25 for a first meeting. Every line cites its sources; lines the critic couldn't source were removed. Research by an AI agent from public web pages: check before quoting.

## Snapshot

- Club Med is a French all-inclusive resort operator headquartered in Paris, not an unrelated firm with a similar name. [1][2]
- Club Med SAS is a subsidiary of Fosun Tourism Group; a Luxembourg holding company sits at the top and holds 99.43% of Club Med Holding. [2][3]
- Sources disagree on the Fosun ownership start date (2013 vs 2015) and on employee count (20,333 vs 29,306). [1][2][3]
- Resort count is commonly cited as over 70 across the Alps, Caribbean, Asia, Americas and Indian Ocean; a 2025 corporate release says 68 premium and luxury resorts in 40 countries; no current count was confirmed. [5][8][9]
- Brands include Club Med Ski (22 ski resorts per one source, 23 per a 2025 release), Club Med Gym, and the Club Med Great Members loyalty program linked to the My Club Med app. [5][6][9][11][12][25]
- Public information on GO community counts and on booking engine, property management system and website tracking is not reliable or not found. [7][26]

## Recent news (last 12 months)

- Club Med set a goal of doubling its size by 2035, with 2.6 million guests across 100 Premium Resorts worldwide. [13][14]
- Club Med announced a new beachfront Exclusive Collection resort in Koh Samui, Thailand, developed with Central Group Capital, dated 20 April 2026. [15][16]
- Club Med announced a comprehensive renovation of Club Med Cherating in Malaysia, closing on 11 October 2026; the completion date has not been announced. [15][16]
- Club Med confirmed it would open its first South African resort on the KZN north coast in July 2026, with a September update. [13][14]

## What guests say (themes)

- Guests praise the kids programs, including baby and petit clubs that accept younger children than many competitors. [18][19]
- Food is frequently praised, though one guest found it mediocre. [17][19]
- Value for money is a recurring complaint: many find the all-inclusive value worthwhile, but some warn of extra costs and high prices relative to quality. [20][21]
- Staff are friendly, but service can be slow and the GO team could be warmer. [17][20]
- Cleanliness and room quality get positive marks, with occasional maintenance issues and some crowding at amenities. [20][21]

## Technology hints

- Club Med partnered with Algolia for site search; the vendor's case study reports more online conversions. [22]
- GM Copilot, a WhatsApp assistant using Microsoft Azure OpenAI with RAG, launched in France on 19 November 2024 and handles 12K monthly conversations across 12+ markets by 2025. [22][23][27]
- Club Med uses the Workday HR suite and 3CX communications, reportedly deployed on Amazon AWS at a South American resort. [23][24][25]

## Ten questions for the meeting

1. How many resorts and guests does Club Med operate today, and which count should we plan against given the 68, 70+ and 100-resort figures in circulation?
2. Which teams own guest-facing digital channels, and how do they split between the website, the My Club Med app and GM Copilot on WhatsApp?
3. How is GM Copilot measured today: resolution rate, handoff to humans, quote conversion, and what happens when it gets an answer wrong?
4. Which languages and markets does GM Copilot cover now, and what is planned as the South African and Thai resorts open?
5. How do guests and staff currently request quotes, changes or complaints during a stay, and where do those requests get lost?
6. What drives the value-for-money complaints: extra charges, pricing transparency, or expectations set at booking?
7. How are GO staff scheduled and supported across resorts, and where do service delays most often happen?
8. How does the Workday HR data feed resort staffing and skills planning, and what is still done by spreadsheet?
9. What does a renovation closure like Cherating involve operationally for bookings, staff redeployment and guest communication?
10. What systems hold booking, property management and loyalty data today, and who owns integration between them, given that public information on these is limited?

## Three use-case hypotheses (4-check test)

| Use case | Why | Felt | Would pay | Buildable in a week | First user known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guest service triage and quote assistant across channels | Club Med already runs a WhatsApp assistant for quotes and questions, and guests report slow service and a warmth gap, suggesting demand for faster, consistent answers. [17][20][27] | Probably | Unknown | Probably | Probably |
| Resort staffing and workforce planning across many sites | Doubling the footprint by 2035 with 100 Premium Resorts makes staffing and skills planning across sites harder, and Workday already holds workforce data. [13][28] | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |
| Value-for-money and pricing transparency for guests | Recurring complaints about extra costs and value for money could be addressed by clearer pricing and upfront cost explanations before and during the stay. [20][21][29] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |

## Outreach email

> Hello,
>
> I am working on understanding how guest service and operations tools are used across Club Med's resorts, and I would like to learn more from people closest to that work. Would you have 30 minutes for a discovery call in the next few weeks? I would like to hear how your teams currently handle guest requests, staffing and pricing questions, and what gets in the way.
>
> I can work around your schedule, and I am happy to send a short list of topics beforehand so the call stays focused.
>
> Thank you for considering it.
>
> Vamsi

# Discovery-prep brief: Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts

Prepared 2026-10-25 for a first meeting. Every line cites its sources; lines the critic couldn't source were removed. Research by an AI agent from public web pages: check before quoting.

## Snapshot

- Four Seasons is a luxury hotel and resort operator headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. [1][5]
- Its most recent release (October 20, 2026) reports 140 hotels and resorts and 61 residential properties in 47 countries. A mid-2026 article gave lower counts (130-plus hotels, 50-plus residences), so the figures vary by date. [5][6]
- It has more than 60 projects under planning or development, including Berlin, a first resort in Okinawa, Jeddah, New Cairo Capital, Diriyah and NEOM. [5][6][7]
- The only employee figure found is roughly 45,000, which is the 2018 headcount. No current employee count or room count was confirmed. [1]
- No reliable public source lists the brand portfolio, the resort versus city-hotel split, or a per-country list of open properties. [1][8]

## Recent news (last 12 months)

- October 2026: a Four Seasons CEO discussed a possible Malta hotel, but no development agreement, location or opening date was confirmed. [12]
- October 2026: the company announced 13 upcoming hotel and resort openings and reopenings across Europe, the Americas, Africa, the Middle East and Asia. [27]
- April 29, 2026: the Four Seasons Hotel Tokyo at Marunouchi began taking reservations for stays after a renovation. [9]
- December 2025: Four Seasons agreed to manage Berlin's Hotel de Rome with Gruppo Statuto, with opening planned for late 2027. [11]
- Management agreement for the Four Seasons Hotel and Private Residences Bengaluru at Embassy ONE is set to end effective 28 February 2027, by mutual agreement with Embassy Group. [10]
- Undated in the findings: Robert Fritz was named Executive Chairman, and Isadore Sharp, Founder and Chairman, will become Chairman Emeritus. [9]

## What guests say (themes)

- Pricing versus value is a recurring complaint, cited at New Orleans and Denver. [14][15]
- Service is the most praised theme, but reviewers also report occasional lapses in attentiveness (Maui, Denver). [13][15]
- Renovation and construction noise is a complaint at some properties, including one Mexico City guest who was not told about remodeling. [18]
- Spa and facilities get mixed reviews: praised at Atlanta and criticized at Vail. [16][17]
- Dining reviews are mixed: breakfast praised in Mexico City, criticized in Kuala Lumpur as buffet-only. [18][19]

## Technology hints

- A June 2020 release describes a guest app for reservations, airport transfers and reaching an on-call concierge. [20][21]
- A Medallia case study describes a regional dashboard report available to every area president and general manager worldwide. [22]
- Sources conflict on AI. A 2017 messaging platform launch was described without chatbots, and another source says service is powered by humans without AI, yet other sources describe an AI chatbot for reservations and recommendations. [20][24][25]
- An AI-readiness consultancy notes that guest preferences may not carry across properties when PMS profiles are not linked upstream. This is a third-party observation, not confirmed company detail. [28]
- No reliable public information was found on the booking engine, property management system, or loyalty platform. [22]

## Ten questions for the meeting

1. Which properties and which teams own guest requests today, and which systems do they use for reservations, transfers and concierge requests?
2. Is there one guest profile across properties, or does a preference captured at one hotel stay there? Which system holds it?
3. Which system is the source of truth for rooms, rates and inventory, and is it hotel-specific or global?
4. What does the current guest app do, and what do guests use it for versus calling or messaging the concierge?
5. What exactly was the 2017 messaging platform, and has any chatbot or AI assistant been piloted or deployed since then?
6. How are guest complaints about value, service lapses and noise captured today, and how do they reach the operations team?
7. How does the Medallia regional dashboard get its data, and who acts on it at the property level?
8. How do general managers decide where to spend on renovation, and how are guests informed while work is underway?
9. Which operational tasks take the most staff time each day at a typical property, and which of them are routine enough to automate?
10. Which upcoming openings, such as Berlin, Okinawa or Jeddah, are most likely to need new systems in the next 12 months, and who would own that work?

## Three use-case hypotheses (4-check test)

| Use case | Why | Felt | Would pay | Buildable in a week | First user known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Concierge triage for routine guest requests | Routine requests such as reservations, transfers and information lookup could be routed or answered first, with staff handling high-touch moments. The findings describe the concierge model and service lapses but say nothing about volume or cost. [13][21][23][24] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |
| Unified guest preference profile across properties | A consultancy notes that a preference recorded at one property may not appear at another when PMS profiles are not linked. This is a third-party observation, so the problem is unconfirmed. [22][28] | Unknown | Unknown | No | Unknown |
| Cross-property guest feedback summarization | Complaints about value, service lapses, noise and decor recur across properties, and a regional dashboard already exists. A tool could group themes and flag issues for area managers. [13][14][15][18][22] | Probably | Unknown | Probably | Probably |

## Outreach email

> Hello, I would like 30 minutes to learn how your guest services and property operations teams handle routine requests today, such as reservations, transfers, concierge questions and guest feedback. I am interested in which systems you use, where the work is slow or repetitive, and what would be most useful to improve first. I would keep the call to what you find useful and make no proposals in advance. Would you be open to a 30-minute discovery call in the next two or three weeks? Thank you for considering it. Vamsi

## Sources

# Discovery-prep brief: Sandals Resorts International

Prepared 2026-10-25 for a first meeting. Every line cites its sources; lines the critic couldn't source were removed. Research by an AI agent from public web pages: check before quoting.

## Snapshot

- Sandals Resorts International (SRI) is a privately held Caribbean hospitality group controlled by the Stewart family, based in Montego Bay, Jamaica. [1][2][3]
- SRI is parent to Sandals Resorts, Beaches Resorts, Grand Pineapple Beach Resorts and The Private Villas Collection. [2][3][4]
- It operates 17 beachfront resorts across eight Caribbean islands; all are adults-only and all-inclusive. [2][8][9]
- Headcount is listed as 10,001+ in one profile and 10,000+ for the Sandals brand on Wikipedia. [2][3]

## Recent news (last 12 months)

- March 2026: SRI committed US$200 million to reimagine Sandals Montego Bay, Sandals Royal Caribbean and Sandals South Coast after Hurricane Melissa; Sandals South Coast reopens November 18, 2026. [13][25]
- October 2026: SRI announced name changes for 15 properties, e.g. Sandals Royal Bahamian is now Sandals Bahamas Nassau. [7][14]
- September 22, 2026: announced that Royal Caribbean Group would take a 50% equity stake in Sandals for $3 billion; one outlet says the deal is close, so its status should be confirmed. [2][5]
- October 19, 2026: Royal Caribbean and Sandals look ahead to the partnership; cruise-and-stay packages and travel advisor perks are planned. [6]

## What guests say (themes)

- Staff are frequently praised as friendly and welcoming. [17]
- Food and drink are praised, though some reviews call buffets or specific dishes 'meh'. [17]
- Pricing and fees are a recurring objection, including an unmentioned service fee, a spa oil charge and a $400 incidental fee at check-in. [17][19]
- Complaints cover restaurant bookings, room condition and butler service. [15][16][17][18]
- Overall online sentiment is largely negative (1.9 stars from 40 reviews, a small and partly undated sample). [16]

## Technology hints

- Infor Hotel Management System and Infor Enterprise Asset Management for Hospitality were adopted to standardize systems, per a case study. [21]
- Unique Travel Corp., the worldwide representative, selected IBS Software's iStay to replace its central reservation system in October 2024. [22][23]
- IDeaS (a SAS company) partnered with Unique Vacations in January 2022 on automated revenue management for Sandals and Beaches. [22][23]
- Sandals Corporate University won a 2025 Brandon Hall award for AI implementation in training, and launched a VR/AR platform with EON Reality. [2][27][28]

## Ten questions for the meeting

1. Which systems does the company run today for reservations, property management and guest service, and which of these are owned by Unique Travel Corp. rather than SRI?
2. What is the current status of the Royal Caribbean deal, and which systems and data would be shared or integrated after it closes?
3. What did the 2025 Brandon Hall award recognize for AI implementation, and which teams use those tools day to day?
4. How are the 15 property renames being rolled out across booking channels, the app and the guest-facing systems?
5. What data is captured about guests during check-in and the guest journey, and where is it stored?
6. How are restaurant reservations handled across properties, and what drives the booking shortages guests report?
7. How are fees such as the service fee, spa oil charge and check-in incidental charge disclosed and recorded in the systems?
8. How is guest feedback collected and routed to operations today, and who acts on it?
9. What does the Infor HMS and EAM rollout look like at each property, and where are the gaps?
10. Which of the reopening properties (South Coast, Royal Caribbean, Montego Bay) are being rebuilt with new systems, and who owns that decision?

## Three use-case hypotheses (4-check test)

| Use case | Why | Felt | Would pay | Buildable in a week | First user known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guest complaint triage and response | Public reviews repeatedly raise service, room and fee complaints, which suggests a support workload that could be sorted and answered faster. [15][16][18][20] | Probably | Unknown | Probably | Unknown |
| Restaurant and app booking assistant | Guests report that restaurants were fully booked and that the app's listings were inaccurate, which points to a booking-accuracy problem. [16][29] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |
| Fee transparency check for bookings and quotes | Pricing and undisclosed fees are a recurring objection, so a tool that checks quotes for all charges before purchase could address it. [17][19][29] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |

## Outreach email

> Hello,
>
> I am reaching out to ask for a 30-minute discovery call about how Sandals Resorts International handles guest-facing operations, including reservations, guest feedback and the systems behind them. I would like to learn where the current workload and pain points sit, and what your teams have already tried.
>
> Would you have 30 minutes in the coming weeks? I can work around your schedule.
>
> Thank you,
> Vamsi

- Hyatt Hotels Corporation (NYSE: H), a global hotel operator headquartered at 150 North Riverside Plaza in Chicago. [4][6]
- Portfolio: 1,528 hotels and all-inclusive resorts with 372,763 rooms as of December 31, 2025 (secondary summary of the FY2025 10-K); more than 1,500 properties in 83 countries as of June 30, 2026. [2][8][9]
- Most rooms are not owned: about 98% are managed or franchised, and the breakdown is 682 managed, 700 franchised, and 28 owned or leased properties. [5][9]
- Roughly 242,000 colleagues at year-end 2025 across corporate, regional and property roles, with about 50,000 directly employed. [3]
- Brands are grouped into portfolios: Luxury, Lifestyle, Inclusive Collection, Classics, and Essentials (Hyatt Select, Unscripted by Hyatt). [2][7]
- I could not find a regional or segment breakdown; the picture here covers totals only. [8][9]

- Q2 2026 results (July 2026): comparable system-wide RevPAR up 5.9%; gross fees up 7.8% to $324M; full-year RevPAR guidance 3.5%–4.5%. Headline-level sourcing, dates not fully confirmed. [10][11][12][13]

# Discovery-prep brief: Club Med

Prepared 2026-10-25 for a first meeting. Every line cites its sources; lines the critic couldn't source were removed. Research by an AI agent from public web pages: check before quoting.

## Snapshot

- Club Med is a French all-inclusive resort operator, now owned by Fosun Tourism Group, running premium beach, island, mountain and selected countryside resorts. [1]
- Club Med SAS is headquartered in Paris, with parent Fosun International. ZoomInfo lists a Miami corporate office, which may be a secondary office. [2][3]
- Headcount estimates conflict: Wikipedia 20,333, PitchBook 28,000, GlobalData 29,306. The company says it employs nearly 25,000 G.Os and G.Es from 110 nationalities. [2][4][5][6]
- The portfolio is nearly 70 premium beach and mountain resorts in 25 countries. Resort counts differ by source: one lists 59 resorts, a 2026 village list shows 61 plus one sailing ship. [6][10][11]
- The group targets 100 resorts by 2035, with 3 to 4 openings a year, and its Exclusive Collection has 21 properties. [12][13]

## Recent news (last 12 months)

- 17 September 2026: Club Med opened its first resort in South Africa, a Beach & Safari property. [16]
- July 2026: the South Africa Beach & Safari resort introduced the brand's first Surf School alongside a safari lodge. [9]
- 21 September 2026: Club Med filed a Hong Kong IPO to grow toward 85 resorts by 2030. [10]
- Club Med Borneo is set to open in November 2026, with bookings having launched on March 24, 2026. [19]
- Club Med and Central Group Capital signed a Hotel Management Agreement for a Koh Samui, Thailand resort, set to open in late 2028. [9][18]
- No reliable public information was found on closures or leadership changes in the past 12 months. The only leadership reference, Stéphane Maquaire, predates this window. [19][20]

## What guests say (themes)

- Staff warmth and friendliness are praised, though slow service is occasionally noted. [21][22]
- Buffet food lacks labelling, and dietary options are not easy to find. [21][23]
- Room readiness and check-in delays recur: rooms ready at 3 PM with a 40-minute wait, or not made up until about 16:00. [29][30]
- Guests report no welcome from a G.O. on arrival at Alpe d'Huez. [31]
- Some guests question value for money, while cleanliness and spacious rooms are praised, with some noting aging furnishings. [21][22]

## Technology hints

- The company has a published partnership with Algolia for search, and an AI-powered search and retrieval engine is reported across 70 destinations in 35 markets. The release is undated. [24][25][26]
- The My Club Med mobile app is listed as a benefit for Great Members. Membership points are credited on booking confirmation. [24][25]
- WhatsApp was integrated into the booking process in Brazil to reach customers where they are active. The date is not known. [27]

## Ten questions for the meeting

1. Which systems hold room status and housekeeping data, and how does that data reach front desk staff on arrival day?
2. What causes the gap between a room being ready at 3 PM and guests waiting about 40 minutes, and who owns that handoff?
3. How do G.Os learn about arriving guests before they reach the resort, and is there a standard arrival-welcome process?
4. How are buffet dietary and allergen details collected and published today, and who maintains them?
5. Which booking channels generate the most volume, and how much of the booking flow runs through WhatsApp outside Brazil?
6. How does the Algolia-powered search relate to the AI search engine described across 70 destinations, and who runs it?
7. What does the My Club Med app do today beyond membership points, and what do guests use it for on site?
8. How do you measure guest satisfaction for value for money, and which feedback channels do you review?
9. How does the team plan the 3 to 4 openings a year toward 100 resorts, and where does onboarding of new properties create the most friction?
10. What did the 2026 openings, including South Africa and Borneo, teach you about tooling for a new property, and what is still unknown?

## Three use-case hypotheses (4-check test)

| Use case | Why | Felt | Would pay | Buildable in a week | First user known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Arrival and room-readiness updates for guests | Reviews describe room delays and missing welcomes at check-in. [29][30][31] | Probably | Unknown | Probably | Unknown |
| Buffet dietary and allergen lookup | Guests say buffet food lacks labels and dietary options are hard to find. [21][23] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |
| Pre-arrival booking and questions assistant on WhatsApp | The company has used WhatsApp for planning and booking in Brazil and aims to reach customers where they are active. [24][25][27] | Unknown | Unknown | Probably | Unknown |

## Outreach email

> Hello,
>
> I'm writing to ask for 30 minutes to learn how your team handles guest arrival, room readiness, and dietary information across resorts. I've read the recent openings and the Algolia and WhatsApp booking work, and I'd like to hear what matters most to your operations team right now and where the current tools fall short.
>
> If a short call next week works, let me know a time that suits you.
>
> Thanks,
> Vamsi

# Discovery-prep brief: Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts

Prepared 2026-10-25 for a first meeting. Every line cites its sources; lines the critic couldn't source were removed. Research by an AI agent from public web pages: check before quoting.

## Snapshot

- Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts is privately held by three shareholders, with Cascade Investment holding the controlling stake (71.25%), Kingdom Holding Company 23.75%, and founder Isadore Sharp's Triples Holdings 5%. [1]
- Headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. [2]
- A January 2026 company release says it operates 135 hotels and resorts and 61 residences in 47 countries; a Wikipedia figure of 133 hotels and 55 residences is undated. [2][3][4][5][11]
- Its target is 180 properties globally by 2033, with a pipeline of more than 60 projects, 65% of which include a residential component. [3][4][5]
- No reliable public information found on room totals, full brand list, or the split between resorts, city hotels and residences; the only employee figure (45,000) dates from 2018. [2][3][4][5]

## Recent news (last 12 months)

- May 2026: Robert Fritz named Executive Chairman; founder Isadore Sharp to become Chairman Emeritus. [6]
- June 2026: Four Seasons and Blasson plan a hotel in Sevilla, set to open in 2028 with 55 rooms in the Arenal Quarter. [6][7][8][9]
- June 2026: Four Seasons Hotel Mykonos, its second hotel in Greece, was set to open in late June 2026 (per a third-party tracker); the company's openings page lists it as now open. [8][9][10]
- 2026 (month not confirmed): Four Seasons with Gruppo Statuto will take over management of Venice's Hotel Danieli after renovations. [10]
- October 20, 2026: development update covering 13 upcoming hotel and resort openings and reopenings for 2027 and beyond. [3][4][5]
- No financial results for the period were found. [6]

## What guests say (themes)

- Staff are frequently praised as friendly, helpful and attentive, and cleanliness is often commended. [12][13]
- Service consistency is a recurring concern: some reviews call it impersonal or inconsistent, and one says it does not justify the pricing. [12][13][14]
- Noise and privacy complaints appear in reviews, including conversations audible next door and construction noise from nearby rooms. [13][15]

## Technology hints

- OPERA Property Management System is selected as the property technology solution for all new Four Seasons properties. [16]
- Guest-facing mobile app launched in 2020 is described as its main digital channel. [19]
- Vendors list Four Seasons as a customer of Canary and Book4Time; the CIO has said Adobe is used for web and Salesforce and Workday are used as enterprise SaaS. [17][18][20]
- Sudhakar Veluru was appointed Executive Vice President and Chief Information Technology Officer. [21]
- Property autonomy may fragment guest profiles, e.g. a preference at one property may not appear at another unless PMS profiles are linked upstream. [22]

## Ten questions for the meeting

1. Which systems hold the guest profile today, and how are OPERA profiles at different properties linked or not linked?
2. How much autonomy do individual properties have over systems and guest data, and who decides?
3. Where does the guest preference data from the mobile app flow, and what does it connect to in OPERA?
4. How are service consistency issues across properties measured today, and who owns that metric?
5. What drives the gap between guest praise for staff and complaints about impersonal service?
6. How are noise and room-privacy complaints tracked, and which teams respond to them?
7. What does the 2027-and-beyond development pipeline mean operationally for systems rollout timing?
8. How are the 13 upcoming openings and reopenings staffed and onboarded, and what tooling is used?
9. Which parts of the Canary, Book4Time, Salesforce and Workday stack are used for revenue and demand forecasting?
10. Which AI tools, if any, are in use today, and who approved and manages them?

## Three use-case hypotheses (4-check test)

| Use case | Why | Felt | Would pay | Buildable in a week | First user known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cross-property guest profile linking | Guest preferences captured at one property may not follow the guest to another, and the portfolio is spread across many autonomous properties. [22] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |
| AI-assisted guest message drafting for staff | Staff could spend more time with guests if drafting emails and responses were faster, and the company describes its service as people-led. [19][24] | Unknown | Unknown | Probably | Unknown |
| Revenue demand forecasting by property, season and segment | A consultancy source lists predictive demand forecasting as an opportunity; this is a general industry idea, not a confirmed Four Seasons deployment. [22][25] | Unknown | Unknown | No | Unknown |

## Outreach email

> Hello,
>
> I am reaching out to ask for a 30-minute discovery call. I would like to learn how guest and operations data currently move between Four Seasons properties and which systems your teams rely on day to day, including OPERA and the guest app.
>
> I am interested in understanding where your teams feel the most friction today and what has been tried so far. I can share what I have learned from public sources beforehand, and I am happy to work around your schedule.
>
> Would a 30-minute call in the next few weeks work for you?
>
> Vamsi

# Discovery-prep brief: Sandals Resorts International

Prepared 2026-10-25 for a first meeting. Every line cites its sources; lines the critic couldn't source were removed. Research by an AI agent from public web pages: check before quoting.

## Snapshot

- Sandals Resorts International (SRI) is a privately held Caribbean hospitality group controlled by the Stewart family. [3]
- SRI is based in Montego Bay, Jamaica, and handles resort development, service standards, training and day-to-day operations. [7]
- The group runs 17 couples-only Sandals resorts across eight islands, plus three Beaches resorts (two in Jamaica, one in Turks and Caicos), Fowl Cay Resort and several private villas. Sources differ on the combined count, with one listing 20 all-inclusive properties across both brands. [2][6][9][10][11][12]
- SRI plans to add 7,000 jobs at new hotels, some outside the Caribbean, which would grow its workforce by more than a third. [5]
- Headquarters details in the source are inconsistent and must be confirmed before the meeting. [8]

## Recent news (last 12 months)

- On September 22, 2026, Royal Caribbean Group was reported to take a 50% equity stake in Sandals and Beaches Resorts for about US$3 billion. [2][4]
- The Royal Caribbean transaction is expected to close in early 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and other conditions. [4]
- On October 21, 2026, SRI announced renamings of 15 best-selling properties, for example Sandals Royal Bahamian is now Sandals Bahamas Nassau. [14][15]
- By October 2026, Royal Caribbean and SRI were describing planned cruise-and-stay packages. [14][15]
- Three resorts are set to reopen in phases toward the end of 2026, starting with Sandals South Coast on Nov. 18, then Sandals Royal Caribbean and Sandals Montego Bay in December. [13]

## What guests say (themes)

- Food is the most frequently praised area, especially sushi, steakhouse dinners and poolside snacks. These are blog-based impressions, not a representative sample. [16]
- Rooms are described as comfortable and well kept, with beachfront and river pool walkouts singled out for praise. [16]
- Breakfast and lunch buffets get lukewarm reviews, often described as fine but unremarkable. [16][17]
- Service quality is uneven: strong in restaurants and weaker at swim-up bars, according to one roundup. [16][17]
- Hurricane disruption produces the most serious complaints, including rebooking windows that guests found restrictive. Value and post-trip service complaints recur on BBB, which lists 142 complaints and no accreditation. [8][18][19]

## Technology hints

- SRI has a strategic plan to standardize 17 properties on Infor's Hotel Management System and Infor Enterprise Asset Management for Hospitality. The source is a vendor announcement. [20]
- A revenue management switch to IDeaS G3 RMS is attributed to UVI, and a 2016 Duetto deal with the same affiliate appears superseded. The link between UVI and SRI is not stated directly. [21][22]
- IBS Software is named for central reservations, PMS and booking engine, but the source does not confirm the month or confirm that SRI uses it. [22]
- A travel guide names Sandals Specialist (sandalsspecialist.com) as the trade booking portal. This is a weak source. [23]

## Ten questions for the meeting

1. Which of the 17 Sandals properties are on Infor HMS today, and what is the timeline for the rest?
2. How are the 17 Sandals and 3 Beaches properties split between separate systems for PMS, CRS and revenue management?
3. Who owns revenue management decisions across islands, and how are rates set and promotions approved?
4. How did the 2025 spring sale and online booking bonus perform, and how do you measure their effect on margin?
5. What did the closure of Beaches Ocho Rios on May 31, 2025 teach you about demand planning for individual islands?
6. How are hurricane-related rebookings handled today, and which teams and systems are involved?
7. Where do you see guest complaints about value and post-trip service being logged and resolved?
8. What does a service standard breach look like in practice, and how is it caught before a guest reports it?
9. How will the Royal Caribbean partnership and cruise-and-stay packages change booking and inventory systems?
10. What would make a first pilot succeed for your operations team, and who would sponsor it?

## Three use-case hypotheses (4-check test)

| Use case | Why | Felt | Would pay | Buildable in a week | First user known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Island-level demand forecasting and pricing support for the 17 Sandals resorts | Eight islands and 17 resorts make island-level demand forecasting relevant, and promotions have been used heavily. Whether the current process is a problem is not established. [24][25] | Unknown | Unknown | Probably | Unknown |
| Guest complaint triage and post-trip service response | Complaints about value, rebooking and post-trip service recur. General industry sources describe AI agents handling routine tasks so staff can focus on complex guest needs. The complaints are individual accounts, not a measured trend. [8][16][17][18][19][28] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |
| Pre-stay preference management linked to room setup | One blog claims pilots link pre-stay survey data to room automation. The claim is unverified and is included only as a hypothesis to test. [27] | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |

## Outreach email

> Hello, I am writing to ask for a 30-minute discovery call about how Sandals Resorts International handles guest operations across its properties. I have read about the Infor standardization plan for 17 properties and the planned Royal Caribbean partnership. I would like to learn how your teams work day to day, which problems matter most, and where current systems fall short. I am not selling anything on this call. I would be glad to work around your schedule over the next few weeks. Would a 30-minute call be possible? Thank you. Vamsi
